questions.question: What is ERB and how do you write it in Rails views?
questions.title: ERB Basics
questions.direct_answer: ERB, or Embedded Ruby, is a template format that combines ordinary text such as HTML with Ruby expressions. In a Rails `.html.erb` view, `<% ... %>` runs Ruby without inserting its result, `<%= ... %>` evaluates an expression and adds its result to the response, and `<%# ... %>` is an ERB comment. Rails escapes unsafe string output by default, so bypassing that protection with `raw` or `html_safe` is safe only for content the application has already sanitised or fully controls.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know <% %> (run, no output) vs <%= %> (run and output), and that <%= %> escapes HTML by default.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using <% %> where you need output (nothing shows), or raw on untrusted content (XSS risk).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: ERB is HTML with Ruby: <% %> runs (no output), <%= %> runs + outputs (escapes HTML by default). Loop with each, output with <%=. Keep views dumb.

sections.title: Quick revision
sections.content:
- `.html.erb` combines an HTML response template with embedded Ruby.
- `<% ... %>` executes control flow or setup without printing its result.
- `<%= ... %>` inserts an expression's result into the response body.
- `<%# ... %>` creates a comment removed during ERB processing.
- Rails escapes unsafe strings by default; do not mark user input HTML-safe.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
ERB means Embedded Ruby. A Rails `.html.erb` file mixes ordinary HTML with small Ruby expressions while the server builds a response. Rails compiles the template and sends only the resulting HTML to the browser; the browser never receives the Ruby source.

Use `<% ... %>` for control flow or setup whose result should not be printed, `<%= ... %>` for a value that belongs in the response, and `<%# ... %>` for a template comment. Opening an `if` or `each` with a control tag and printing only the needed values keeps the output intentional.

A list view can open a loop with `<% products.each do |product| %>` and place `<%= product.name %>` inside each list item. The control tag decides how many fragments are built; the output tag supplies the visible value. Calling `puts` inside the template does not insert that value into the HTML response.

Rails HTML-escapes ordinary unsafe strings placed through an output tag, so a product name containing markup is shown as text. `raw` and `.html_safe` bypass that protection and must not be applied casually to user input. ERB should describe presentation and call view helpers; data loading and business rules belong outside the template.

sections.title: ERB compiles a template into response-building Ruby
sections.content:
A template is not sent to the browser as Ruby source. Rails compiles the ERB into a method that appends static text and evaluated output to a buffer. By the time the client receives the response, only the resulting HTML remains.

Control-flow tags shape which static and dynamic fragments reach that buffer. They can open a Ruby block in one tag and close it later because the generated method contains one continuous Ruby program. Output tags append a value after converting it for the response context.

HTML safety is contextual. Escaping converts characters such as `<` into text-safe entities so a value is displayed rather than treated as a tag or script. Sanitising is a separate operation that allows only an intended subset of markup. Marking an unsafe value as safe skips the guard without cleaning it.

A view can call helpers for links, formatting, tags, and localisation. Queries or multi-step domain decisions inside the template are harder to reuse and can create hidden performance problems, especially when a loop triggers database access for every row.

sections.title: Choose the ERB tag by output behaviour
sections.content:
| Tag | Runs Ruby | Inserts a value | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<% ... %>` | Yes | No | `if`, `each`, assignment |
| `<%= ... %>` | Yes | Yes | text, helper result, rendered partial |
| `<%# ... %>` | No application expression | No | template-only comment |
| `raw(value)` / `value.html_safe` | Yes | Unescaped | only trusted or sanitised markup |

sections.title: Use control tags for the loop and output tags for values
sections.content:
```erb

Products

<% if @products.empty? %>

No products yet.

<% else %>
    <% @products.each do |product| %>
  • <%= product.name %>
    • <% end %>
<% end %> <%# This comment is absent from the HTML response. %> ```
